query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases is governed by selective oxidation or reduction of Al and Ti at grain boundaries and phase interfaces, leading to embrittlement and catastrophic intergranular failure. The governing behavior can be revealed by varying the partial pressure of oxygen or hydrogen during exposure and observing changes in grain boundary chemistry and mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with fcc matrix, as-built microstructure.
generation.intervention: Expose samples to elevated temperatures (e.g., 800–1000°C) under controlled atmospheres with varying partial pressures of O2 (oxidizing) or H2 (reducing).
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature (800–1000°C), controlled gas atmosphere (O2 or H2), exposure times sufficient for observable degradation (e.g., 10–100 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundaries and phase interfaces in the fcc matrix, with possible segregation of Al and Ti.
generation.mechanism: Selective oxidation (in O2) or reduction (in H2) of Al and Ti at grain boundaries leads to formation of brittle oxides or intermetallics, causing loss of cohesion and promoting intergranular fracture.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increasing O2 partial pressure will increase Al/Ti oxide formation at grain boundaries, leading to greater embrittlement and lower fracture toughness. Increasing H2 partial pressure may promote reduction and destabilization of protective oxides, also leading to embrittlement. Catastrophic failure is expected when grain boundary degradation reaches a critical threshold.
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties and microstructure of the as-built alloy before exposure; minimal grain boundary oxidation or embrittlement.
generation.boundary: Applicable for elevated temperatures (800–1000°C) and atmospheres with significant O2 or H2 partial pressure; not applicable at low temperatures or inert atmospheres.
generation.uncertainty: Exact critical partial pressures and exposure times for catastrophic failure are uncertain due to lack of direct evidence; role of minor phases or precipitates is not fully resolved.

falsification_experiment.design: Expose alloy samples to a range of O2 and H2 partial pressures at 900°C for 50 hours. Characterize grain boundary chemistry (e.g., TEM/EDS, XPS), measure fracture toughness and observe fracture surfaces (SEM).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If grain boundary oxidation/reduction does not correlate with embrittlement or catastrophic intergranular failure, or if mechanical degradation occurs without grain boundary chemical changes, the hypothesis is falsified.
